Hi, I'm a neuroscientist studying how the brain encodes, learns, and adapts. That started during my undergraduate and graduate researches on various brain disorders — PTSD, stroke, Alzheimer's disease — then moved into sensory perception and learning. My current work is on the [Cell Types & Learning project](https://www.allenneuraldynamics.org/projects/cell-types-learning) at Allen Institute / Neural Dynamics, linking spatial transcriptomics to _in vivo_ neuronal activity during task learning.

Increasingly, that work involves developing algorithms for data acquisition, processing, and QC, deploying pipelines to scale, and building ML and agentic AI methods to make sense of large-scale, multimodal neuroscience data.

Recent focus areas:

- _In vivo_ two-photon imaging, spatial transcriptomics, multimodal data integration (neuronal activity, behavior, gene expression profile)
- Role of inhibitory interneurons in sensory perception and learning
- Building image data processing, QC, and analysis pipelines
- GCaMP8 transgenic mice validation and characterization
- Agentic AI-assisted pipeline development
